subject: Throughput SLO vs memory tilt — GPU selection & reserved-commit sizing for Quantify
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@quantifylabs.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GPU guidance: throughput SLA + memory-heavy context — help?

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Quantify is finalizing the architecture for our inference tier and we need help choosing the right Dedicated pool mix. A few constraints:

- Production throughput target: 180–220 QPS sustained (peak bursts to 300 QPS) for our multi-tenant chat endpoints.
- Model mix: 70% short-turn assistants (single-turn, 1–2k tokens), 30% long-context summary jobs (8–16k tokens) and embeddings batch jobs overnight.
- Memory sensitivity: the long-context jobs regularly need 60–70GB KV/cache per instance.
- Cost sensitivity: target perf/$ improvement vs our current cloud-hosted endpoints — ideally 2x better.

We ran a quick micro-benchmark (attached quantify_benchmark.csv) showing H100 ~1.9x raw token throughput vs our baseline A100-40GB for the long-context model, but the A100-80 (when available) closes the gap on some workloads. L40S looked cheaper for embeddings but has less headroom for long-context.

Can Redwood recommend a recommended pool composition (counts and GPU types) for a 12‑month reserved commit with throughput SLAs? Also what discount bands make sense at ~400 GPU-hours/month sustained? We want a clear tradeoff: latency SLOs, perf/$, and how much headroom we need for canary/rolling upgrades.

Appreciate any ballpark numbers and a sample commit structure to review with procurement.

Best,
Emma
Emma Jones
Head of Platform
Quantify Labs

Attachments: quantify_benchmark.csv, architecture_diagram.pdf

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: GPU guidance: throughput SLA + memory-heavy context — help?

Emma — great detail, thanks. Pushed this to Karthik for sizing and Marcus for commercial options; initial read below.

High-level recommendation (short):
- Hybrid pool: mix of H100-80GB + A100-80GB, with a small L40S band for embedding-only workers.
- H100 nodes: optimize for long-context steady workers (60–80GB KV/cache headroom). A100-80 as the cost-efficient baseline for the 1–2k token traffic.
- Suggested starting composition for your target QPS (estimates): H100: 6 nodes, A100-80: 10 nodes, L40S: 2 nodes. This assumes load balancing by route and autoscaling-driven hot swap for bursts.

Notes and open q's:
- We need to validate your token-per-second distribution for the long-context jobs — if those are extremely bursty you may need additional headroom for concurrent KV caches.
- Perf/$: H100 gives the best token throughput on long-context but is ~30–60% higher unit cost vs A100; net perf/$ can still favor H100 for memory-heavy workloads because A100 can require more nodes to match latency SLOs.
- Commit sizing: a 12‑month reserved commit at the 400 GPU-hours/month baseline gets us into a moderate discount band; we can show ~20–28% list reduction depending on how much burst buffer you keep uncommitted.

I've attached a quick sketch of the sizing rationale. Karthik — can you drop numbers for steady-state throughput and a sample commit cadence? Marcus — can you advise discount tiers we can offer for a 12‑month vs 24‑month commit and what flexibility we can provide around burst capacity?

Thanks,
Neha
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks Neha/Emma — dug into the attached benchmark and ran a couple of quick estimators against Redwood's serving profiles. Notes below (TL;DR numbers at the top):

- Ballpark steady-state for 200 QPS target: ~ (6 H100-80GB equiv) + (9 A100-80GB equiv) to hit 95th pct latency <= 250ms on mixed workload. L40S: 2 nodes for embedding batching (cheaper perf/$ for embed-only jobs).
- If you prioritize strict 95th pct latency for long-context requests, add +1-2 H100 nodes as headroom.
- Perf/$: measured perf/$ improves when using H100 for the long-context bucket because it reduces the number of concurrently pinned KV caches; example: for the long-context profile, H100 delivered ~1.8x tokens/sec per dollar vs A100-40 in our test.

Assumptions I used (please confirm):
- Avg long-context concurrent requests: 18–25 during peak (from your SRE notes).
- Long-context average generation length: 9k tokens; short-turn average: 1.5k tokens.
- Embedding batch jobs run in 3 overnight windows (low priority).

Recommended commit structure (starter):
- 12-month reserved commit: guarantees 420 GPU-hours/month (sustained) split as 60% A100-80 equivalent, 35% H100-80 equivalent, 5% L40S. This lets you run with our suggested mixture and have a 15% burst buffer.
- Discount bands: list-level reduction tiers we typically offer: 0–199 GPU-hrs: standard list; 200–499: ~18–24% off list; 500–999: ~25–33% off list. Exact % depends on billing cadence and overage pricing.

Operational points:
- Autoscaling policy: keep autoscale headroom for canary traffic on the A100 band to reduce risk during rollouts; long-context traffic should be routed to H100 when KV/cache > 48GB to avoid cache thrash.
- Canary / rollback: recommend canary on 1–2 A100 nodes first, then H100. We support automatic fallback to A100 variants if H100 is unavailable, but latency will increase for long-context routes.

Emma — if you can share a short sample of request distribution (tokens per request histogram), I can produce a tighter node-by-node estimator and an expected monthly bill delta vs your current hosted spend.

-karthik

Emma — thanks for the detailed ask and the benchmark. Commercials and a concrete offer below.

Offer summary (12-month term, payable monthly):
- Reserved commit: 480 GPU-hours/month (baseline). Allocation guidance: 55% A100-80 equiv, 40% H100-80 equiv, 5% L40S.
- List-equivalent pricing (example): A100-80 list $X/hr, H100-80 list $Y/hr, L40S list $Z/hr.
- Proposed blended discount: 26% off list for the 12-month commit with a 10% top-up discount on committed overage if you pre-commit to a minimal burst buffer (we can structure a 3-tier burst allowance).
- Flexibility: quarterly revisit for rebalancing GPUs between types; we allow one swap window per quarter without penalty.

Why this structure: it buys you a predictable baseline while keeping a small, managed burst buffer for peak events. The higher H100 allocation vs Karthik's starter list is because we want to reduce tail-latency risk for the long-context bucket and minimize additional A100 nodes that would increase perf/$ inefficiency.
